title: Extraction and Quantification of Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Silages by RP-HPLC-DAD
author: Julián ndrés Castillo Vargas

steps.title: Thaw frozen samples
steps.instruction: On the day of analysis, thaw the frozen silage samples at room temperature (20 °C).

steps.title: Weigh silage
steps.instruction: Weigh exactly 10 g of fresh silage and transfer it into a glass‑jar blender.

steps.title: Add Milli‑Q water
steps.instruction: Add 100 mL of Milli‑Q water (measured with a class A volumetric pipette) to the glass‑jar blender.

steps.title: Blend mixture
steps.instruction: Blend the mixture for 30 s at an intermediate speed.

steps.title: Vacuum filter mixture
steps.instruction: Filter the blended mixture using a PYREX™ Gooch‑type filtering crucible together with vacuum‑filtration equipment; retain the liquid filtrate.

steps.title: Prepare extraction mixture
steps.instruction: Combine filtrate with extraction solution and homogenise.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 2 mL of the filtrate into a 6 mL plastic centrifugation tube.
Add 2 mL of the extraction solution (as described in section 3.1).
Vortex the tube for 30 s at an intermediate rate.

steps.title: Centrifuge extraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 10 000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect and filter supernatant
steps.instruction: Recover the liquid phase, filter it, and collect the final extract.

substeps.instruction: Using a plastic syringe, withdraw a portion of the supernatant after centrifugation.
Pass the withdrawn liquid through a 0.45 µm PES membrane filter.
Collect at least 500 µL of the filtered extract in a chromatographic vial.

steps.title: Prepare calibration curves
steps.instruction: Prepare calibration curves for lactic acid and the short‑chain fatty acids (SCFAs) according to the procedures described in Materials sections 3.3.1 and 3.3.2.

steps.title: Run calibration samples
steps.instruction: Analyze each point of the calibration curves using RP‑HPLC‑DAD under the method conditions.

steps.title: Inject sample extracts
steps.instruction: Place 500 µL of the final silage extract into a chromatographic vial (if not already done) and load it onto the RP‑HPLC‑DAD system.

steps.title: Set chromatographic parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the HPLC system with the following conditions:

substeps.instruction: Column temperature: 30 °C.
Injection volume: 20 µL.
Stationary phase: Hypersil GOLD C18 column (150 × 4.6 mm) with Hypersil GOLD C18 guard column (10 × 4 mm).
Detection wavelength: 210 nm.
Flow rate: 0.750 mL/min (gradient mode, see Figure 3).

steps.title: Mobile phase and column notes
steps.instruction: Observe the following constraints when preparing mobile phases and running the method:

substeps.instruction: The secure pH range for the Hypersil GOLD C18 column is 2 – 8; avoid buffers outside this range.
Do not use 100 % aqueous mobile phases (e.g., pure inorganic‑acid solutions) because the column does not tolerate them.
The C18 column separates most SCFAs efficiently, but butyric and iso‑butyric acids show limited resolution; iso‑butyric acid is usually low in silage, allowing acceptable estimation of butyric acid.

steps.title: Allocate protocol timing
steps.instruction: Plan the approximate duration for each stage of the workflow:

substeps.instruction: Mobile‑phase reagent preparation: 10 min (for 50 samples).
Sample preparation (steps 1‑8): 30 min per sample.
Calibration‑curve preparation: 242 min for 50 samples.
HPLC‑DAD set‑up and stabilization: 15 min (for 50 samples).
HPLC‑DAD sample run time: 22 min per sample.
Data analysis: 5 min per sample.
